A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GTR-Turbo research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original training results, benchmark comparisons, and ablations on Points24 and ALFWorld, including the Qwen3-VL experiment in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original Points24 and ALFWorld results and reports additional comparisons, analyses, and an Android-in-the-Wild experiment.

M1.justification: Checkpoint merging with TIES, SMA/EMA weighting, and the SFT and reverse-KL guidance variants remain unchanged. Equations and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same training procedures. Testing alternative merging frequencies does not replace the proposed default procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Android-in-the-Wild GUI control using Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (Appendix C.2), substantially extending coverage beyond card arithmetic and embodied household tasks. Points24 and ALFWorld remain; Qwen3-VL evaluation on ALFWorld already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds static-base-model KL regularization and rejection sampling as evaluated self-improvement comparators in Figure 6. Its new Android-in-the-Wild comparison includes DigiRL alongside PPO (Table 6). These extend the comparator set, while membership in the original benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include pass@k comparisons through k=32, GPT-5.2 judging of reasoning quality, static-teacher controls, and merging intervals of five and ten epochs. These substantially broaden the evaluation procedures. Existing training budgets, initialization descriptions, and Table 5 hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds controls testing checkpoint merging against static regularization and rejection sampling. Appendix C.3–C.5 adds analyses of sampled base-model capability, merging-frequency sensitivity, and reasoning quality during training. The earlier TIES, guidance-range, KL-estimator, and SMA/EMA studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Shaded training curves remain without definitions of their bands; v2 introduces no explicit change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values. New Table 6 reports Android-in-the-Wild success rates of 80.2% for GTR-Turbo, 75.0% for PPO, and 71.9% for DigiRL, with reasoning scores of 3.93 versus 3.26 for GTR-Turbo and PPO. New controls and appendix analyses add further findings. Conversely, v2 removes two ablations' episode-return panels and shortens the displayed Qwen3-VL trace from 20,000 to approximately 15,000 steps; these are reporting omissions, not demonstrated performance declines.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, merging formulas, KL estimators, and environment reward equation are retained. Neither version supplies formal theoretical results or proofs, and the new pass@k interpretation does not introduce a formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a merged-checkpoint teacher providing efficient, self-contained thought guidance. The abstract retains the same performance and efficiency claims. Mentioning Qwen3-VL in v2's introduction foregrounds an experiment already present in v1's appendix.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations that merging provides more than static regularization, RL exploration explains the advantage over rejection sampling, and pass@k results indicate capabilities beyond the base distribution. Reasoning ratings support a stronger teacher-quality interpretation. Section 3.4 replaces the capability-dependent stabilization rationale with an efficiency-focused motivation, and the conclusion adds an initial success rate below 5% as a failure-condition example.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code repository link, specifies 40GB GPU memory, and explicitly identifies the KL variant for the retained Qwen3-VL ALFWorld experiment. These are additional disclosures; the pseudocode, training-data sources, and hyperparameter table remain unchanged. Repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Qwen3-VL, ProAct, rejection-sampling-related research, and evaluation of capabilities beyond the base model. These provide limited extensions to the positioning; the established related-work organization around agent training, process guidance, and model merging remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence largely remain. v2 copyedits the prose, rewrites the KL-guidance motivation, reorders ablation discussions, and moves supplementary experiments before environment descriptions. Author affiliations and footnotes change, and an acknowledgment is added.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the predominantly single-column report layout with a two-column main text, revises framework diagrams to show task/format prompts, and adds four analysis figures and Table 6. Existing displays are resized and relocated; two ablations lose episode-return panels, and the Qwen3-VL plot shows a shorter horizon.

improvement.justification: The new static-teacher and rejection-sampling controls, merging-frequency tests, and GUI evaluation strengthen the empirical case beyond v1. The gain is limited by sparse Android-in-the-Wild and GPT-5.2 judging details, and by interpreting finite pass@k saturation as a capability ceiling. Useful additional evidence and code-access information outweigh the limited loss of plotted results, producing a modest net improvement.
